segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Next up, whatever the ultimate state of their equity looks like, Open AI is closing a deal to stand up 10 gigawatts of data center capacity.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Sources told The Information that Open AI is in advance negotiations to lease A10 GW data center campus to be built on federal land in Ohio.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The campus is expected to cost $500 billion based on current pricing for chips, labor, and power.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: This would make it not only Open AI's largest data center commitment to date, but likely the largest data center campus ever built. 10 gigawatts is roughly 4 1/2 times the total output of the Hoover Dam and more than the capacity of the largest nuclear power plants operating in the US.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Sources said that NVIDIA is attached as a financial backer and the current structure of the deal would see open AI lease the chips as well as the facilities.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: They wouldn't be required to begin repayments until the 1st GP US are powered up.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: With 800 megawatts expected to come online in 2028.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The total life of the lease could be as long as 20 years.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: And while one of the critiques of NVIDIA in the past has been participating in some sort of circular financing deals, they haven't previously backstopped any data center deals whatsoever, let alone one of the size.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Instead, the deal has echoes of Project Stargate, which was announced at the beginning of 2025 but stalled out earlier this year.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Stargate was originally intended to be a $500 billion joint venture with Oracle and SoftBank, who appear to be playing a role in this new deal as well.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The site in question is a decommissioned uranium enrichment facility in Pike County, Ohio, around 50 miles South of Columbus.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The federal government will own the power plant, with SoftBank subsidiary SP Energy functioning as the plant operator.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Now, while it appears that the project is being designed to preempt the major sources of data center outrage, local politics are still turning sour.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Controversy erupted this week in Cleveland when legislators discovered their previous governor had signed deals with Amazon, Meta and Google to provide 100% sales tax exemptions on data center operation lasting for 40 years.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: While the deal made Ohio an attractive destination for new data centers and has already brought in 10s of billions in investment, the state estimates the deals will cost 1.8 billion in lost tax revenue.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: And as one report states, given the uncapped nature of the tax exemption, final numbers could be significantly higher.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Democrat Representative Tristan Radar told local press.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: I'm just dumbfounded.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: This is so poorly designed.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The tech companies saw fertile ground and have been taking advantage of US ever since.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Meanwhile, overall bands and moratoriums are increasingly on the table as data center resistance grows.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: New York looks set to become the first state to hit pause on new data center construction after passing a one year moratorium late last week.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The bill would block any new permits for data centers above 20 megawatts, which is obviously very small scale for AI infrastructure.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: State Senator Kristin Gonzalez, the lead sponsor of the bill, argued that New York's constrained and aging grid can't keep up with the pace of construction.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Almost 10 gigawatts of new facilities are currently seeking approval.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Next up, we wait to see whether New York Governor Kathy Hochul will actually sign this one.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The city of Seattle followed suit on Tuesday, with City Council unanimously approving A1 year ban on new data centers as well.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The proposal came after the Seattle Times reported that five proposed data centers could consume up to 1/3 of the city's electricity.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Interestingly, the opposition in this case was driven by tech workers themselves, with groups including Amazon Employees for Climate Justice mounting letter writing campaign.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The reasoning was a little garbled, with a spokesperson for climate group 350 Seattle claiming tech workers organized against the data centers because, quote, AI is synonymous with people losing their jobs.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: The antipathy towards data centers has even reached Texas, with Governor Greg Abbott calling for stronger consumer protections against rising electricity costs.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Abbott directed state utilities to require new data centers to fully fund additional infrastructure needed for their operations to ensure the costs aren't passed to ratepayers.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: In addition, Abbott unveiled a wide-ranging regulatory agenda for consideration in next year's state legislative session, including mandatory closed loop cooling systems, annual reporting of water and electricity use, and a requirement for data centers to add new electricity generation to the grid.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Now to be honest, if you are a person who thinks on the one hand the single fastest way towards guaranteed AI inequality is data center moratoriums.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: But on the other hand completely recognizes communities not wanting to foot the bill for increased electricity costs along with dealing with other type of negative externalities of data centers.

segments.speaker: OpenAI's Ohio Data Center and Growing Public Resistance
segments.text: Then looking to a place like Texas, which is a very popular destination for new data center construction, to lead the way in setting standards for what that construction should look like is kind of optimistic.
